verdict: valid failure, of one part on a two-part plate
printer: Prusa CORE One+ (HF0.4), Prusament PLA, 0.20mm BALANCED, camera via go2rtc (1280x720)
times: local, MDT (UTC-6); the history and Obico scores are in UTC
part: the same spaghetti-two-stage.gcode as spaghetti-small-nest (see its make_plate.py), run a second time: a small block whose floating slab falls as a nest, beside a large 40 x 25 x 22 mm block

fault.how: the small block's floating slab (Z10.2-11.6) prints into the air and falls on the small block; a strand trails to the front edge of the bed
fault.persists_until: never, but it stops growing once the slab's layers are done: from about p45 the debris is static and only the large block is printing

what_it_looks_like: strands falling from the slab at p39, a nest on the small block with one strand to the bed's front edge by p41, then the same debris unchanged in every frame to p76 while the large block grows cleanly

acceptable: acknowledge-failure watch, after looking again and seeing the debris static and the printing part clean (what the agent did)
pause, then acknowledge-failure stop with an escalation, because one part on the plate has failed and a person should decide
never: a fan, speed, flow or temperature change: none reaches strands already on the bed
cancel: the agent's policy does not grant it
expected_agent_action.why: only a warning, and the debris is not growing; the part still printing is sound. Whether a half-failed plate is worth finishing is a person's call, so either carrying on watched or holding it for a person is defensible

detector.note: the second run of this file never crossed Obico's pause threshold, where the first (spaghetti-small-nest) did. Scores fell back to 0 once the head moved to the large block, and stayed at 0 through the whole overnight stall that followed (see filament-stall-air-print). Rows 7-12 (22:21-22:23) are a warm-up false positive boxing the toolhead
